findings.title: The `deleteMany` OR's second branch has no method or date filter, so it deletes non-SMS and future-scheduled reminders
findings.description: The new `OR` clause adds `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` as a standalone branch. Only the first branch restricts `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` and `scheduledDate <= now`. The second branch matches every `WorkflowReminder` with `retryCount > 1`, regardless of `method` (email, WhatsApp, and so on) and regardless of `scheduledDate` (including reminders scheduled in the future that are still valid). The original query was scoped to past-due SMS reminders, so this change widens a destructive delete well beyond its intent. The retry condition needs to be nested inside the SMS and past-date conditions, for example as an `AND` of all three.

findings.title: The `retryCount` update in the `catch` block can throw and escape the per-reminder loop
findings.description: The new `prisma.workflowReminder.update` call sits inside the `catch` block, outside any `try`. If the update fails (for example, because the reminder was deleted mid-run or the database is unavailable), the exception propagates out of the `for` loop and aborts processing for all remaining reminders. The `console.log` that follows is never reached. Wrapping the update in its own `try`/`catch`, or moving it so a failure cannot abort the loop, would prevent this.

findings.title: The retry threshold is `gt: 1`, so reminders are deleted at `retryCount` 2, not after a single retry
findings.description: A reminder is incremented once per failed attempt. Deletion happens when `retryCount > 1`, so the effective number of attempts before deletion depends on how many runs occur before the check. Confirm that `gt: 1` matches the intended retry limit.
